title: abelmoschus strictus
intro: Abelmoschus strictus, commonly known as the 'Indian mallow' or 'Kashmira', is a plant species native to India and parts of Asia. It has been traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine for its health benefits, including the treatment of fever, digestive issues, and inflammation, due to its therapeutic actions such as anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antipyretic properties. The bioactive constituents present in Abelmoschus strictus include flavonoids, glycosides, and phenolic compounds, which contribute to its medicinal properties. The plant's leaves, flowers, and roots have been utilized in various forms, including teas, infusions, and extracts, for their potential health benefits and therapeutic applications.
